children: The FTSE 100 fell around 0.5% to a seven-week low in afternoon trading on Thursday, as Brent crude surged above $105 a barrel after Iran warned it was prepared for a more intense conflict.
Mining stocks came under heavy pressure, with Antofagasta and Anglo American falling more than 5%, while Endeavour, Glencore and Rio Tinto each declined by more than 3%.
Associated British Foods was also among the biggest losers, dropping over 9% after Primark sales came in weaker than expected and the group outlined plans to demerge the retailer by December 2027.
Energy stocks provided some support, with BP gaining 2% and Shell rising 1.8% as higher oil prices boosted the sector.
Meanwhile, the European Central Bank raised interest rates by 25 basis points, in line with market expectations.
The ECB also lifted its inflation forecasts and warned that price growth is likely to remain above its 2% target for an extended period.

title: FTSE 100 Falls to 7-Week Low
